correctness.rationale: The signed Catalan interval recurrence follows bijectively by pairing the first vertex and splitting the remaining interval. A C++17 complete combination/orbit enumeration checks all 64+2016+41664+635376 supports with distinct orbit sizes and finds 544 zeros at degree four, divided into 256 stars and 288 brooms in 17 size-32 dihedral orbits. Independent Python inclusion-moment enumeration over all 1430 Catalan matchings yields identical results; both actual source checkers ran with exact integer markers. For every even n>=4 the reflection-paired Catalan weights give precisely half the matching mass and the star count is injective by its center. No higher-order or unproven infinite lower-bound claim is made.

value.rationale: This completes a natural low-order Fourier cancellation layer of the convex Catalan matching codebook: none of the 3-or-fewer chord parity tests is unbiased while exactly 544 fourth-order tests are; they form only 17 full geometric symmetry orbits of two support-graph types. The 288 broom cancellations are not a mere restatement of the elementary universal 256-star construction. The exact finite cutoff and even-size construction are structurally motivated by parity-test recoverability and Catalan matching symmetry, not arbitrary data slicing.
